pull.title: KAFKA-21227: Speed up ColdStartStickinessIntegrationTest
pull.body:
The classic protocol case of ColdStartStickinessIntegrationTest takes
about
73 seconds locally, while the streams protocol case takes about 23
seconds.
After the first phase, the test closes both instances and waits for the
group to become empty before the cold restart. With the classic
protocol,
the stream threads stay in the group on close, so the group only becomes
empty when both members are removed on heartbeat expiration, about 44
seconds after the close (the default 45 second session timeout). The
streams protocol case is not affected, because dynamic members leave the
group on close by default.

This sets session.timeout.ms to 6 seconds and heartbeat.interval.ms to 1
second for the classic protocol case, so the members expire shortly
after the first phase closes. The instances still close without leaving
the group. Closing with LEAVE_GROUP does not work here, because the
first instance's LeaveGroup triggers a rebalance that can assign its
tasks to the second instance before it closes, which creates extra state
directories.

Local runs of the classic protocol case on the same machine:

| | Before (2 runs) | After (10 runs) |   |---|---|---|   | Test time
|72.8s, 72.9s | 33.8s to 34.0s |

All runs passed. In these runs, the first phase closed in under 1
second, and the members expired about 5 seconds after that.

repo.name: kafka

reviews.body: Thanks for the patch. Could you take a look at the failing test in CI?

issue_comments.body:
> Thanks for the patch. Could you take a look at the failing test in CI?

Thanks for checking. The failure was caused by this change. With
LEAVE_GROUP, the first instance's LeaveGroup triggered a rebalance while
the second instance was still running, so the second instance was
assigned all four tasks and created state directories for the first
instance's two tasks (6 instead of 4).

I've restored the original close and instead set a 6 second session
timeout and a 1 second heartbeat interval for the classic case. Locally,
the classic case takes about 34s (73s before) and passed in all 10 runs.
I couldn't run it on Java 25 locally, so I'll keep an eye on CI. I've
also updated the description.

@m1a2st Gentle ping. The CI failure is fixed, and all checks pass on the latest commit.
Instead of using LEAVE_GROUP, the fix now shortens the session timeout for the classic case,
bringing the local runtime down from about 73s to 34s.
Could you take another look when you have time? Thanks!
